The matter was mentioned before Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant before advocate Nizam Pasha. The CJI agreed to hear the case this week. Chief Justice of India Surya Kant Khan and his son Abdullah Azam were granted bail by the Allahabad High Court in the dual PAN card case on October 29. The High Court suspended Khan's 10-year sentence in the dual PAN card case but refused to stay his conviction. Khan and his son were released from Rampur jail on October 31 but Khan was detained by the ED team waiting outside the jail. The ED action came in relation to a separate money laundering case involving alleged financial irregularities concerning Mohammad Ali Jauhar University. A special Prevention of Money Laundering Act (PMLA) court in Ghaziabad remanded Khan to 14-day judicial custody on Sunday, November 1. IFF is a digital rights advocacy organisation that defends against threats to civil liberties and democracy in India, and SFLC is a donor-supported legal services and policy organisation founded in 2010 that protects digital freedom, privacy and civil liberties in India. The IFF on Tuesday, November 3, said it would approach the court if the Delhi Police does not withdraw the notices, which also seek removal of 37 posts, including content published by 16 other users. IFF said it received copies of the two police notices from X on the morning of November 3. The notices were filed by the Special Commissioner of Police (Crime), Delhi Police, on October 31 and November 2, 2026. According to IFF, the first notice was submitted to X on October 31 at 8.06 pm. items.title: Bloodstains, empty classrooms and fear: Andhra school struggles after chainsaw attack
items.summary: The haphazardly discarded shoes, scattered books and lumps of partly dried blood are enough to send a chill down anyone's spine. Inside this classroom at the Zilla Parishad High School in Rapthadu in Andhra Pradesh’s Anantapur district, a 21-year-old man walked in carrying a chainsaw and attacked a 15-year-old girl, leaving her critically injured. Another student who tried to protect her was also wounded. The brutal attack on October 31 has since triggered outrage across the state. The classroom remains closed as a crime scene. But the evidence of the horror that unfolded here is still visible. The blood splattered across the floor, the belongings left behind in haste and the images of the attack offer a grim reminder of what the students and teachers witnessed. On October 31, at around 10.30 am, while a lesson was underway, the accused, identified as Hemanth alias Dummu, entered Class 10 carrying a running chainsaw and attacked Gopika, a student. She suffered severe injuries to her face, neck and abdomen, and her right hand was nearly severed. Lakshmi, another student, was injured when she tried to intervene and save her friend. Hemanth fled the school, leaving the chainsaw behind

items.title: Kerala High Court Justice Bechu Kurian Thomas completes Ironman 70.3 triathlon in Goa
items.summary: In what is likely a first for the Indian judiciary, sitting High Court judge, Justice Bechu Kurian Thomas , completed the gruelling Ironman 70.3 triathlon which was held in Goa this past weekend. An Ironman 70.3, also known as a Half Ironman, is organised by the World Triathlon Corporation. The 70.3"refers to the total distance in miles (113.0 km) covered in the race, consisting of a 1.2-mile (1.9 km) swim, a 56-mile (90 km) bike ride, and a 13.1-mile (21.1 km) run. Kerala High Court judge Justice Bechu Kurian Thomas competed in the men's 55-59 years category and completed the race with a time of 8:46:44. In an affidavit filed in the Court, the government said that Krishi Bhawan and the Central Secretariat complex are secular premises dedicated exclusively to governmental, administrative and public service functions. It added that there is a mosque located at India Gate in the two kilometre radius. items.title: Mercedes crash: Kerala court to hold in-camera hearing of appeals against bail granted to accused minor
items.summary: A sessions court in Kerala on Monday decided to hold in-camera hearings of the appeals against the bail granted to the minor accused of driving a Mercedes-Benz car and killing a scooterist. The 17-year-old accused, the son of an additional district judge, was driving a Mercedes-Benz car when he hit a two-wheeler in Kochi's Cheranalloor in the early hours of October 25, killing the scooterist, one Jayabalakrishnan. Ernakulam Additional District and Sessions Judge Kavitha Gangadharan on Saturday criticised the police for not acting against social media posts that revealed the minor's identity. Section 74 of the Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act, 2015, prohibits the disclosure of the identity of a child in conflict with law (CCL), except with the permission of the competent authority. The Court had, therefore, directed the cyber police to take action against all posts revealing the teenager's identity. When the appeals moved by the State and the victim's family against the bail granted to the minor was taken up today, the Court deemed it fit to continue the hearing in-camera, to further ensure the privacy of the Child in Conflict with the Law (CCL). items.title: Indian scientist secures patent for in-vivo power generator after Bombay High Court order against IIT
items.summary: The Indian Patent Office has formally approved a patent for scientist Dr. Tarkeshwar Chandrakant Patil, securing his exclusive ownership over an invention capable of generating electrical power inside the human body. This outcome follows a September 8 order of the Bombay High Court in Patil’s decade-long dispute with the Indian Institute of Technology (IIT) Bombay. The dispute involved an apparatus and a method for in-vivo power generation, a technology designed to keep medical implants active inside the human body. Patil’s patented device functions by converting glucose found in cerebrospinal fluid into a hydrogen-rich fuel, such as ethanol or methanol, using bioenzymes. This fuel powers a nano-scale biofuel cell implanted in the body, creating a self-sustaining power source that mitigates the need for repeated surgeries to replace traditional lithium-ion button batteries. IIT Bombay initially filed the patent application in August 2013. However, after internal disputes, the institute executed a worldwide assignment deed in 2017 transferring all intellectual property rights to Patil. items.title: How Bengaluru’s drag performers are building community, one song at a time
items.summary: Izzy B is a 26-year-old drag queen born and raised in Bengaluru. Drag was not something she had set out to do. It was her curiosity about queer spaces that led to her first queer party in 2022. “I saw these beautiful queens, dressing up, with wigs and beautiful makeup, lashes and everything, and I was fascinated,” she says, recalling the first few drag performances she witnessed. Izzy started loving the art form when she saw another drag queen, Cologne Doll, perform. “I saw her on the stage of Kitty Ko (a queer-friendly nightclub in Bengaluru), and I was like, this is so good, I love it.” Drag is a performance and visual art, rooted in queer subculture. Drag performances often involve exaggerated traditional gender expressions to challenge the same. Performances usually feature drag queens or drag kings who dress in clothing associated with the opposite sex or otherwise. Performers choose a drag name or a stage name based on their interests and build a unique drag persona. A drag performer can be cis, trans, non-binary, or any sexuality; the persona performed on stage can also differ from how someone identifies off stage.
